review: RM-401 transaction retry candidate and coupled RM-207 boundary matrix
scope: Independent contract and saved-evidence review only; no generated adapter implementation or production retry conformance claimed

accepted_findings.finding: The retry gate correctly requires a listed transient cause, proved no commit, a repeatable outer effect graph, and remaining shared budget. SQLite rollback after commit-time SQLITE_BUSY and PostgreSQL 40001/40P01 server aborts have representative saved evidence. An unclassified transport failure after possible COMMIT remains unknown and cannot be replayed.
accepted_findings.limit: The probe uses a diagnostic driver harness on Bun 1.2.20, not generated adapters; it does not prove every network timing, SQLITE_LOCKED, or production replay case.

accepted_findings.finding: TIME-D05 requires a fresh stable wall-clock snapshot for each retry attempt, shared by nested calls within that attempt. The logical delivery identity and monotonic deadline stay shared. The candidate follows this rule and correctly allows a retry across an expiry boundary to change the domain outcome.
accepted_findings.limit: The retry_clock_refresh assurance case is a future RM-402 requirement; the present generated runtime captures one request operation context and has no retry loop.

accepted_findings.finding: The Bun HTTP 500 outcome_unknown envelope is an explicit adapter choice. A read that fails before any possible write or external dispatch has no effect and must not be classified OutcomeUnknown. The current unknown-read test validates only envelope containment.

required_changes.finding: The shared proof rule in operational-boundary-v0.1.json requires proved no effect or no commit for every retry, but failure-model.md section 7.1 says job defects receive bounded runtime retry and RateLimited, Unavailable and TimedOut follow declared retry policy without stating the proof condition. A defect or timeout can occur after a write or provider dispatch, so literal job wording permits unsafe replay.
required_changes.proposed_change: Qualify section 7.1 so job retry policy is subordinate to the same certainty, repeatability, identity and budget gate. Persist uncertain delivery state and reconcile without automatic resend when an effect may have occurred. Keep defect alert/dead-letter behaviour but do not retry a possibly committed defect.

required_changes.finding: The classification table's broad 'rollback proof fails' row maps to OutcomeUnknown even when the adapter can independently prove no transaction began or no effect was possible. OutcomeUnknown is reserved for an effect that may have committed or been accepted.
required_changes.proposed_change: Make the unknown branch conditional on a possible effect or commit. A failed rollback with independent no-effect proof remains a safe operational failure, with no automatic retry unless its cause is listed transient and the ordinary retry gate holds. State the evidence precedence for failed BEGIN, read-only, and pre-dispatch paths.

implementation_gates_for_rm402.finding: Generated PersistenceFaultKind currently has driver/constraint/cardinality/unknown only. PostgreSQL begin() callback errors are returned directly; SQLite rollback failure replaces the original error. Neither path carries the phase/outcome proof required for automatic replay.
implementation_gates_for_rm402.proposed_check: Record authentic structured server errno plus transaction phase and terminal rollback/commit evidence. Preserve both original and rollback faults internally. Treat an unresolved rollback after an effectful callback as unknown unless the server independently proves abort.

implementation_gates_for_rm402.finding: The saved probe proves representative driver behaviour but not a generated route, separate-process contention, safe in-flight deadline/cancellation handling, nested replay budget, exactly one outbox intent, or refreshed operation time.
implementation_gates_for_rm402.proposed_check: Run the RM-402 two-adapter injection matrix on generated output, including an in-flight commit timeout/cancellation that preserves unknown outcome, as well as the specified rollback, clock-refresh and identity assertions.

implementation_gates_for_rm402.finding: The shared semantic failure checker still assigns HTTP 500 to OutcomeUnknown, while the accepted contract has no cross-adapter HTTP default.
implementation_gates_for_rm402.proposed_check: Remove the shared default during RM-207 implementation while retaining the explicitly selected Bun envelope and its route/OpenAPI/audit parity checks.

correction_review_2026_10_02.scope: Independent re-review of the B1 and B2 corrections; historical findings above remain the original review record

resolved_findings.evidence: failure-model.md section 7.1 now subordinates every job retry, including a defect retry, to proved no effect/no commit, repeatability, stable delivery identity, a transient cause and remaining budget. Possible dispatch/commit retains uncertain state through lease expiry and restart. operational-boundary-v0.1.json now includes job_defect_after_possible_dispatch with no automatic retry.

transaction-retry-plan.md now limits rollback-failure OutcomeUnknown to cases where an effect/commit remains possible and gives independent pre-BEGIN/read-only/pre-dispatch no-effect proof precedence. operational-boundary-v0.1.json adds cleanup_failure_without_effect with a conditional retry gate.

correction_review_2026_10_02.time_semantics: The revised text does not alter TIME-D05: each attempt still receives a new stable operation snapshot; nested calls share the attempt snapshot, while the logical identity and monotonic deadline remain common.
correction_review_2026_10_02.remaining_limits: Approval is for the shared contract and RM-401 freeze only. The saved Bun/SQLite/PostgreSQL diagnostic probe remains representative driver evidence; current generated adapters still lack phase-aware retry classification and the RM-402 conformance matrix. RM-207 still needs actual provider/transaction/job integration, route/OpenAPI/audit parity and recovery evidence.
correction_review_2026_10_02.nonblocking_editorial_note: The matrix-level proof_rule could mention stable logical identity explicitly to mirror section 7.1; existing provider and transaction cases already require it, so this is not a freeze blocker.
validated: Read the corrected failure-model.md section 7.1, transaction-retry-plan.md classification and precedence text, and new matrix cases
